newsitem.title: USA: Sprint Q3 long-distance income up.
newsitem.headline: Sprint Q3 long-distance income up.

text.p: Sprint Corp said Tuesday its long distance operating income increased 32.4 percent to a record $242 million from $183 million in the 1995 quarter.
Call volume in the third quarter increased 21 percent compared with a year ago, and was up four percent from the second quarter, Sprint added.
This volume growth exceeds the 19 percent posted in the second quarter of 1996 and is the highest for the company since the 1980s, Sprint said.
However, volume growth exceeded revenue growth by four percentage points because of a change in mix of services provided, a dynamic expected to persist in the fourth quarter.

"We currently expect to once again report double-digit volume and revenue growth for our business consumer and wholesale segments in the fourth quarter," chief financial officer Arthur Krause told a conference call.
Operating margins for the long distance operation were 11.6 percent in the third quarter, up a shade from 11.5 percent in the second quarter but strongly ahead of the 10.0 per cent of a year ago.
Sprint's operating margins were 16.9 percent, up from 16.6 percent the prior quarter and 15.5 percent a year ago.
Earnings per share at $0.72 were one cent below analysts consensus forecast according to First Call.
Sprint said that excluding start-up losses for Sprint Spectrum PCS and Global One, earnings per share were up at $0.83 from $0.77 a year earlier.

Krause noted that the company's performance included weathering a two percentage point increase in its tax rate and a 24 percent increase in shares outstanding, as shares were issued to bring its European partners' stake up to 20 percent.

For Global One, an international venture with the partners, Deutsche Telekom DTK.CN and France Telecom, Sprint's portion of operating losses in the quarter was $24 million, or $0.04 per share. For wireless venture Sprint Spectrum it was $48 million or six cents per share.
"Global One has achieved initial sales results well ahead of our expectations," Krause said.
Krause said annualised sales at Global One would be $1 billion by the end of this year.

Sprint said its capital spending for the year is projected at $2.2 billion, with a $350 million investment in Sprint Spectrum mostly completed. No further investment in Global One was expected for the year.

Local telephone operating income rose 16.5 percent from a year ago, and the number of customer lines grew 5.4 percent from a year ago, to exceed seven million. Local telephone revenues grew 11.4 percent to $1.31 billion from a year ago.

The company said its competitive local telephone access services were moving ahead, and it expected to begin by reselling the lines of incumbent local telephone companies before later moving to own the facilities.
Sprint said data services performed particularly strongly in the quarter, with revenues up 20 percent from a year ago, and frame relay doubling in the period.
The shares were $3/8 ahead at 40-1/4 in mid-morning trade. -- Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712
